_doc: Shared lookup fixtures for data/universes.json. BOTH catalogs run these against their OWN implementation of the lookup, and both must return the same answer. This is the mechanism PLATFORM.md §5.3 prescribes for a rule that has to exist in Python and in TypeScript: pin it with one fixture file rather than hope two implementations agree.
_whyThisExists: §2.3 of PLATFORM.md records the drift bug this repo has already shipped once — resolve_author_link (Python) and _resolveAuthorFolder (JS) split author strings the same way until they did not, and a promote failed silently. The universe lookup is the same shape of hazard: a pure function that must give one answer in a Python static build and in a TypeScript Worker. There is no shared runtime, so there is no shared implementation; the fixtures are what keeps them honest.
_contract: Each case gives `title` and `series` exactly as a catalog row carries them, and `expect` is the canonical universe name or null. The resolution order under test is data/universes.json `_lookup.order`. `author` is informational and is NOT part of the key today — recorded because the pen-name evidence under Runnerverse may make it part of the key later.

cases.name: the mixed series, the member that IS in the universe
cases.title: Tress of the Emerald Sea
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: Secret Projects 1. Answered by a bookOverride, not by a series — the row carries no series at all.

cases.name: ⚠️ the mixed series, the member that is NOT — the case that kills series-keying
cases.title: The Frugal Wizard’s Handbook for Surviving Medieval England
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: Secret Projects 2, the one of five that is not Cosmere. A bookExclusion. ⚠️ The title carries a CURLY apostrophe (U+2019) — a lookup that does not fold it returns the wrong answer here and nowhere else, which is the worst possible place for a normalisation bug.
cases.measured: audiobook_catalog site/catalog.csv, 2026-08-11: title exactly 'The Frugal Wizard’s Handbook for Surviving Medieval England', series blank.

cases.name: the same exclusion written with a straight apostrophe still excludes
cases.title: The Frugal Wizard's Handbook for Surviving Medieval England
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: Pins the apostrophe folding in the other direction. The library catalog and the audiobook catalog do not agree about quote characters, so both spellings must resolve identically.

cases.name: ⚠️ the seriesless trilogy — Otherlife 1
cases.title: Otherlife Dreams - The Selfless Hero Trilogy
cases.author: William D. Arand
cases.why: The second case that kills series-keying, from the opposite direction: the trilogy name lives inside the title and the series field is empty, so a series-keyed lookup misses it entirely.
cases.measured: audiobook_catalog site/catalog.csv, 2026-08-11: all three Otherlife rows have a blank series.

cases.name: the seriesless trilogy — Otherlife 2
cases.title: Otherlife Nightmares - The Selfless Hero Trilogy
cases.author: William D. Arand
cases.why: Same as Otherlife 1.

cases.name: the seriesless trilogy — Otherlife 3
cases.title: Otherlife Awakenings - The Selfless Hero Trilogy
cases.author: William D. Arand
cases.why: Same as Otherlife 1. Sorts first alphabetically and is volume 3, which is why seriesToCreate records the reading order.

cases.name: ⚠️ the seriesless standalone that IS in a universe — Fires of December
cases.title: Fires of December
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: The third case. No series, not part of any series, and unambiguously Cosmere — publisher copy calls it 'a standalone Cosmere novel'. THE example of the owner's rule that a universe says something the series name does not.
cases.measured: No row in audiobook_catalog site/catalog.csv as of 2026-08-11 — it is a library/pledge item. The lookup must still answer correctly for a title that only one catalog holds, which is the whole reason the list is shared.

cases.name: a plain series match
cases.title: The Way of Kings
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: The ordinary path — step 3 of the resolution order. Most rows land here.

cases.name: ⚠️ Secret Projects as a series value resolves to NOTHING
cases.title: Some Secret Project
cases.why: 'Secret Projects' is a real series value in the audiobook catalog and is deliberately absent from The Cosmere's series list, because four of its five members are Cosmere and one is not. If it ever appears in a series list, this case fails and the Frugal Wizard becomes wrong.
cases.measured: audiobook_catalog site/catalog.csv, 2026-08-11: series 'Secret Projects' exists on one row.

cases.name: an exclusion beats a series that would otherwise sweep it in
cases.title: Lux - A Texas Reckoners Novel
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: Reckoners is in The Cosmere's notSeries, and this title is an explicit exclusion. Both must say no; the order (exclusions first) is what makes the answer independent of which rule fires.

cases.name: same author is not a universe
cases.title: Steelheart
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: The seed refusal 'Same author, different world'. notSeries records it; the lookup must return nothing rather than falling back to the author.

cases.name: The Last Horizon is in the Willverse — the refusal was answered
cases.title: The Captain - The Last Horizon, Book 1
cases.author: Will Wight
cases.why: ⚠️ This case ASSERTED THE OPPOSITE until 2026-08-12, and the flip is the point. It began as the owner's 'leave blank for now' when the multiverse was only hinted at. It stayed null through a second pass, when the named continuity was established but the household appeared to own just one member series — and a universe spanning one series says nothing its own name does not. It became Willverse only once The Last Horizon was confirmed as Iteration 119 (Fathom), giving two owned series to span. A refusal is a decision, and so is reversing one.

cases.name: Turncoat's Truth IS in the Runnerverse — co-authored, and still inside it
cases.title: Turncoat's Truth - Turncoat's Truth, Book 1
cases.author: William D. Arand, Victor E. Krabin
cases.why: ⚠️ This case ASSERTED NULL until 2026-08-12. It was held out because the book is CO-AUTHORED with Victor E. Krabin, and a collaboration does not reliably sit inside an author's own continuity — the same rule that keeps The Reckoners out of the Cosmere. The owner verified and it does. Kept as a case precisely because the co-author makes it the one Arand series a reader would expect to be excluded.

cases.name: The Axe Falls stays OUT — settled, and under its REAL series spelling
cases.title: The Axe Falls - The Axe Falls Series, Book 1
cases.author: William D. Arand
cases.why: ⚠️ SETTLED 2026-08-12, not pending: the owner looked for a link and found none — 'leave both out, i cant find any connections.' A single-book series offers no cross-series evidence, leaving only the author, which is never sufficient here. ⚠️ Keyed on 'The Axe Falls Series', which is the actual value in site/catalog.csv — the refusal prose says 'The Axe Falls', and a held-out series keyed on the wrong string would hold nothing out.

cases.name: children's picture-book lines are never a universe
cases.title: Bizzy Bear: Fire Rescue
cases.why: The loudest possible false positive — the library catalog is mostly children's books. A brand is not a continuity.

cases.name: cross-catalog: the only universe present in both
cases.title: The Lightning Thief
cases.author: Rick Riordan
cases.why: The one universe that spans both catalogs. The same title exists as an audiobook and as an Illumicrate hardcover; both must resolve to the same universe, which is the point of one shared list.

cases.name: an unknown series is not a universe
cases.title: Something Nobody Catalogued
cases.series: A Series Nobody Has Heard Of
cases.why: Default-deny. An absent answer is the correct answer; guessing is what the whole file exists to prevent.

cases.name: an empty row resolves to nothing rather than throwing
cases.why: Both pipelines hand rows in with blank fields routinely. A crash in the universe layer would take a build down over a field nobody asked about.

cases.name: Cradle is in the Willverse
cases.title: Unsouled
cases.author: Will Wight
cases.why: The second owned member series. Cradle alone would not have earned the universe — this pairing with The Last Horizon is what did.

cases.name: Cultivating Chaos stays OUT — the VeilVerse in its title is a hint, not evidence
cases.title: Cultivating Chaos - VeilVerse: Cultivating Chaos, Book 1
cases.author: William D. Arand
cases.why: ⚠️ SETTLED 2026-08-12, not pending: the owner looked for a link and found none — 'leave both out, i cant find any connections.' A single-book series offers no cross-series evidence, leaving only the author, which is never sufficient here. ⚠️ Its title names a 'VeilVerse', which is NOT the Runnerverse. That is exactly the kind of plausible-looking label this list refuses to act on unverified — and if the VeilVerse is ever confirmed it would be a NEW universe, not an addition to an existing one.

cases.name: Tailored Realities is NOT the Cosmere — Sanderson, and that is the trap
cases.title: Tailored Realities
cases.author: Brandon Sanderson
cases.why: ⚠️ SETTLED 2026-08-12: the owner confirms it is specifically NON-Cosmere short fiction. Tested because it is the second-most likely false positive in the whole list — a Sanderson collection sitting among ten Cosmere rows, with a blank series so nothing else contradicts a careless guess. The Frugal Wizard's Handbook is the first, and it already has its own case.

cases.name: cross-format: a board game is Marvel by title override, not by series
cases.title: Dice Throne: X-Men
cases.why: The first cross-format universe answer this file pins. Resolved by the bookOverride on the exact title, never by the series — see the next case.

cases.name: ⚠️ 'Dice Throne' as a bare series resolves to NOTHING — the mixed series that proves the game side needs the same rule as the book side
cases.title: Dice Throne: Alchemist
cases.why: Same shape as 'Secret Projects': most Dice Throne content (Vanguard, Outcasts, Season One/Two ReRolled, Mystic Brawler, Alchemist, Santa vs Krampus, Slam Throne) has no Marvel connection at all, so the series is deliberately NOT claimed by Marvel. If this ever resolves non-null, every non-Marvel Dice Throne row in the catalog just got swept in by mistake.

cases.name: a Marvel game accessory needs its OWN override — the resolver never inherits from parent_item_id
cases.title: Marvel Dice Throne: Hero Sculpt - Thor
cases.why: Board-game rows carry a parent_item_id tree (base → hero expansion → sleeves/sculpt/playmat) but universeFor() resolves per row on title+series alone — it does not walk the tree. Every accessory needed its own exact-title override for the same reason the accessory itself needed its own row in board-game D1.

cases.name: Star Wars split out of Disney — crossover-potential criterion
cases.title: Star Wars: Light of the Jedi - The High Republic
cases.why: ⚠️ This case ASSERTED 'Disney' until 2026-08-15, same day: the owner's actual criterion arrived ("universes are defined by CROSSOVER POTENTIAL — Star Wars and Toy Story would never cross over, but games like Kingdom Hearts would cross over with Toy Story") and Star Wars failed Disney's own bar, so it was split into its own universe, the same treatment Marvel got. Claimed at series level because 3 owned rows share this exact series value.

cases.name: Toy Story stays IN Disney — it's the pool Kingdom-Hearts-style crossovers draw from
cases.title: Toy Story 1 - Disney Classic Stories
cases.why: The contrast case for the Star Wars split: Toy Story passes the owner's crossover-potential test (Kingdom Hearts-style media plausibly draws on it), Star Wars does not. Both were reachable from 'Disney' before 2026-08-15; only one still is.

cases.name: Shards of Creation is The Cosmere — the Shards of Adonalsium
cases.title: Shards of Creation
cases.why: Owner, 2026-08-15, via coordinator: 'literally all the gods from the cosmere.' Publisher Brotherwise Games, same as the already-claimed Cosmere RPG line and Mistborn deckbuilder. Series is null, so a title override.

cases.name: Alliances — owner-approved universe, not folded into Marvel
cases.title: Stan Lee's Alliances: A Trick of Light
cases.why: Owner, 2026-08-15, via coordinator: 'your ready-to-apply option is approved.' Confirmed NOT Marvel canon (POW! Entertainment original) in this session's first pass — see Marvel's watch note.

cases.name: ⚠️ Devil's Quintet stays in NO universe — a real series, one owned volume, correctly filed already
cases.title: Stan Lee's The Devil's Quintet: The Armageddon Code - A Novel
cases.why: Confirmed 2026-08-15 as a genuine 2-book series (Book 2, The Shadow Society, published 2023 — https://www.goodreads.com/series/363085-stan-lee-s-the-devil-s-quintet) with only Book 1 owned. Its series field is already correct in site/catalog.csv (curly apostrophes, U+2019) — nothing to fix — and one owned volume of a real series does not earn a universe under this file's own rule.

cases.name: ⚠️ 'The Cosmere' as a bare series is NO LONGER claimed — owner-revised order 5
cases.why: ⚠️ This case ASSERTED 'The Cosmere' until 2026-08-15, same day: the owner first said leave the series field alone and just match it, then REVISED that — blank the series non-destructively and match by title instead. 'Cosmere'/'The Cosmere' were only ever claimed as series because of the two specific rows below; now that both are fixed at the source, re-claiming either spelling as a series would silently sweep in anything else that happens to carry it, which is exactly the failure mode this file's own notes on The Cosmere used to warn about from the other side.

cases.name: The Emperor's Soul is The Cosmere by TITLE now, not by its old series value
cases.title: The Emperor's Soul
cases.why: library_catalog id 30. Used to carry series 'The Cosmere' (a universe masquerading as a series); the field is now blanked non-destructively (change_log preserves the old value) and this exact title is an override instead — the owner-revised order 5 outcome.

cases.name: same case, the sibling row — 'Cosmere' with no article, also now a title override
cases.title: Shadows for Silence in the Forests of Hell
cases.why: library_catalog id 25. Used to carry series exactly 'Cosmere' (no leading article); now blanked the same way as The Emperor's Soul, id 30.

cases.name: Arcanum Unbounded is The Cosmere by title, series corrected to blank — order 7b
cases.title: Arcanum Unbounded: The Cosmere Collection
cases.why: Owner, 2026-08-15, via coordinator: 'Arcanum should be in no series since it's in all the series and is just cosmere' — an anthology of 9 Cosmere stories across Elantris/Sel, Mistborn and Stormlight (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arcanum_Unbounded:_The_Cosmere_Collection). audiobook_catalog's series field was WRONG ('The Mistborn Saga') and is corrected via the corrections layer (ASIN B01K5Q6VWO) to blank; this title override is what catches it now.

cases.name: Disney — a seriesless Disney Books imprint title needs its own override
cases.title: Disney Junior Ariel: A Magical Mess
cases.why: The Disney Books imprint rows all carry a blank series, the same shape that forced per-title overrides for Otherlife and Secret Projects on the book side.

cases.name: the Divine Dungeon board game joins CAL Verse, not a new universe
cases.title: Divine Dungeon the Game
cases.why: canonicalNames already folds 'divine dungeon universe' onto CAL Verse and 'The Divine Dungeon' is already a claimed series there — direct evidence a standalone Divine Dungeon universe was considered and declined before. The game's series is null, so it needed its own title override to land the same place its books already do.
cases.measured: board-game D1, id 103, publisher Mountaindale Press, 2026-08-15.

cases.name: cross-format: the Cosmere RPG line joins The Cosmere by title override
cases.title: Cosmere RPG: Stormlight Handbook
cases.why: Brotherwise Games' officially licensed Cosmere RPG line. Every row's series is null, so each of the 21 RPG products plus the Mistborn deckbuilder needed its own override — the same exact-title-only rule as every other Cosmere case above.

canonicalNameCases.why: The owner's spelling wins. Required by _decided.canonicalNames.
The name the model reaches for. Required by _decided.canonicalNames.
Evidenced by Solaria's own `naming` note — naming it after one of its two series was considered and rejected.

Named in The Cosmere's notes as a real but UNLISTED universe. An unknown name normalises to nothing; it must not be invented, and it must not fold into The Cosmere just because that entry mentions it.

_knownGaps.gap: ⚠️ 'Isles of the Emberdark - A Cosmere Novel Secret Projects, Book 5' does not resolve
_knownGaps.detail: The audiobook catalog holds TWO rows for this book — 'Isles of the Emberdark' (series blank) and 'Isles of the Emberdark - A Cosmere Novel Secret Projects, Book 5' (series 'Secret Projects'). The bookOverride matches the short title only, because title matching is exact by design (see _lookup.exactTitlesOnly). The long row therefore resolves to no universe.
_knownGaps.whyNotFixedHere: Two candidate fixes and both belong elsewhere. Adding a second override would put a damaged row title into the decisions file and would change the owner's stated count of ten Cosmere overrides. Loosening to substring matching would make 'Elantris' match 'The Hope of Elantris'. The right fix is an entry in audiobook_catalog scripts/catalog_overrides.json correcting the row's title — the layer that exists for exactly this — after which the override matches with no change here.
_knownGaps.notAsserted: Deliberately NOT a fixture case, because a case asserting null here would enshrine an answer that is wrong about the book.

_knownGaps.gap: The library catalog's own rows were not measured
_knownGaps.detail: Every `measured` note above cites audiobook_catalog site/catalog.csv, which is a file on disk. library_catalog's rows live in remote D1 and were not queried while this file was written, so the exact series spellings on the library side — 'Cradle' in particular — are asserted from the owner's wording, not observed.
